question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Coromandel Factories — Location]
options: Masulipatnam (Machilipatnam) — Located on the Coromandel coast in present-day Andhra Pradesh
Masulipatnam — First English factory on the eastern (Coromandel) coast of India, established in 1611
Fort St. David — English fortification near Cuddalore, also on the Coromandel coast
Masulipatnam — Located on the Malabar coast in present-day Kerala, at the mouth of the Periyar River
wrong_fact: Masulipatnam is NOT on the Malabar coast. It is on the Coromandel coast in the Krishna delta region of Andhra Pradesh. The Malabar coast is in Kerala, and the Periyar River is a Keralite river unrelated to Masulipatnam.
explanation: Masulipatnam (modern Machilipatnam) is situated on the Coromandel coast in the Krishna district of present-day Andhra Pradesh. The English established a factory there in 1611, making it the earliest English factory on the eastern coast. Fort St. David near Cuddalore (Tamil Nadu) was another Coromandel coast installation. The Malabar coast runs along southwestern India (Kerala), and the Periyar River flows through Kerala — neither has any geographic link to Masulipatnam.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Coromandel Factories — Trade Goods & Context]
options: Masulipatnam — Major centre of Indian cotton textile (particularly chintz) exports to Southeast Asia and Europe
Golconda Sultanate — The regional power under whose jurisdiction Masulipatnam fell before Mughal annexation
Masulipatnam — Dutch, English, and French all had competing factories here at different times
Masulipatnam — Part of the Carnatic Nawabship and never under Golconda or Mughal rule
wrong_fact: Masulipatnam WAS under the Golconda Sultanate before the Mughals annexed the sultanate in 1687. It was not simply a Carnatic entity — Golconda (and then Mughal) jurisdiction preceded any Carnatic Nawab arrangement.
explanation: The Golconda Sultanate (Qutb Shahi dynasty) controlled the Krishna-Godavari region, including Masulipatnam, until Emperor Aurangzeb conquered Golconda in 1687. Subsequently the region came under Mughal authority and later evolved under the Nizams and Carnatic Nawabs. European powers — Dutch, English, and French — all competed for factories at Masulipatnam. Masulipatnam's chintz exports to Southeast Asia were especially significant. The claim that it was 'never under Golconda' is historically incorrect.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Coromandel Coast — Geography & Factory Network]
options: Coromandel Coast — Stretches from the mouth of the Krishna River in the north to Point Calimere (Kodikkarai) in the south
Pulicat — Site of the Dutch headquarters (Geldria) on the Coromandel coast, also briefly an English post
Armagaon (Armagon) — Attempted early English settlement on the Coromandel coast before Masulipatnam
Coromandel Coast — Runs along the western shore of the Indian peninsula facing the Arabian Sea
wrong_fact: The Coromandel coast faces the BAY OF BENGAL (eastern shore), NOT the Arabian Sea (western shore). The Arabian Sea coast is the Malabar/Konkan coast.
explanation: The Coromandel coast is the southeastern coast of India, running from the Krishna delta region (Andhra Pradesh) down to Point Calimere in Tamil Nadu, facing the Bay of Bengal. It is NOT on the Arabian Sea side. The English attempted an early settlement at Armagaon (Armagon) before shifting operations to Masulipatnam (1611) and then to Madras (1639). Pulicat (north of Madras) was the Dutch headquarters in South India. The Arabian Sea side of India is where the Malabar and Konkan coasts are.
